summary: Editorial review of six analysis/scan figures. The three module EnergyScan canvases are commendably consistent (shared energy palette teal/gold/red/blue/black/purple for 1/3/5/7/9/11 GeV, shared response y-range 0-13500 per EnergyScan*.C:237, identical panel grammar), but carry two systematic production defects: (1) CRITICAL - the response-panel y-axis tick labels "12000" and "10000" are clipped to "2000"/"0000" at the pad edge in ALL THREE figures (5-digit labels do not fit the 0.125 left margin set in macros/radStyle.h:32); (2) MAJOR - the known house issue of in-frame subtitles colliding with content is live in every timing panel: the DrawLatex(0.16,0.86) subtitle (EnergyScan.C:295 and clones) sits on top of the teal fit curve and the 1 GeV markers. Additionally the timing panels clip data: the frame is sized by the median graph only (gt->Draw("AP") with no SetMaximum, EnergyScan.C:275-280), so the LuAG 1 GeV mean marker is half-cut by the top frame and the DSB1 1 GeV mean marker is entirely absent - silently missing data. A cross-figure semantics problem: open markers mean three different things in this figure family (mean-of-capillaries estimator, 11 GeV low-purity demotion via the unlegended demote11 overlay at EnergyScan.C:239-246, and raw-vs-centered in SaturationStudy) - at 11 GeV in a timing panel, black-open (demoted median) and grey-open (mean) are distinguishable only by outline colour. XCETScan clips the 1 and 3 GeV electron peaks at the x=900 edge of the right panel and has an unexplained stray red mark at ~(272 ADC-eq, 3%) in the left panel. SaturationStudy lists a 9 GeV legend entry with no visible curve. DriftStudy panel 2's in-frame label strikes through a tick mark, and the figure lacks the one annotation that would make its argument - a shared vertical guide at the ~9 h gain/noise onset. All files are raster PNG at ~250 dpi equivalent; journal production would require vector (PDF/EPS) export. Captions/annotations are factually accurate against the documented campaign results (quadrature fit form confirmed in code: sqrt(a^2/E+b^2), EnergyScan.C:287-289) with two annotation-vs-content mismatches flagged (dead 9 GeV legend entry; "plateau = clean tag" while the 7-11 GeV cuts visibly sit on steep slopes, which is honest but unremarked).

plots.what_it_shows: LuAG:Ce 6-point energy scan, 2x2 canvas: (1) tagged-electron Sum-LG spectra per energy with event counts, (2) response linearity vs beam energy with dashed linear-through-5-GeV reference, (3) sigma/E vs energy, (4) srCFD 4-cap shower-time sigma vs energy with median (filled) and mean (open grey) estimators plus teal quadrature fit a/sqrt(E) (+) b anchored on the 1 and 9 GeV medians.
plots.caption_issues: In-figure annotations are factually correct: 'dashed: linear through 5 GeV' matches the code (EnergyScan.C:249-250, slope pkE[2]/E[2]); 'width (position-smearing dominated)' matches the documented finding; open 11 GeV markers match the documented purity caveat. Gaps a journal would flag: (a) the 11 GeV open-marker demotion (demote11 lambda, EnergyScan.C:239-246) is applied in panels 2-4 but explained NOWHERE on the figure - and in panel 4 it collides semantically with the legend's 'mean of capillaries' open marker, so at 11 GeV black-open (demoted median) vs grey-open (mean) differ only by outline colour; (b) the fit form is quadrature - TF1 'sqrt([0]*[0]/x+[1]*[1])' at EnergyScan.C:287-289 - but no panel annotation states the form or fitted values (389 (+) 138 ps), and the summary-text convention 'A/sqrt(E)+B' reads as a linear sum; state 'a/sqrt(E) (+) b' with numbers on-panel; (c) 'srCFD' jargon undefined in-figure; (d) no on-figure caveat that the response panel's above-line 7/9 GeV points are the documented +/-15% cross-run gain ladder, inviting a false nonlinearity read without the SaturationStudy companion.
plots.design_issues: 1. CRITICAL (production): response panel (top-right) y tick labels '12000' and '10000' are clipped to '2000' and '0000' at the pad's left edge - a reader takes wrong numbers off the axis. Cause: 5-digit labels vs SetPadLeftMargin(0.125) and y-title offset 1.55 (radStyle.h:31-38) with SetMaximum(13500) (EnergyScan.C:237). Fix: widen left margin to ~0.15, or relabel axis in units of 10^3 ('Sum LG peak [10^3 ADC-eq]'), or SetNdivisions(505). 2. MAJOR: timing panel (bottom-right) - subtitle 'srCFD 4-cap shower time (incl. MCP+DRS)' (EnergyScan.C:295, DrawLatex 0.16,0.86) is overprinted by the teal fit curve and the 1 GeV median marker sits inside the text; the 1 GeV open mean marker (~440 ps) is half-clipped by the top frame because the frame is autoscaled to the median graph only (gt->Draw('AP'), no SetMaximum; gm drawn 'P same' at line 280-281). Fix: gt->SetMaximum(1.15*max(median,mean,fit@1GeV)) and move the subtitle above the frame or into the vacant top-right area. 3. MINOR: response panel top half (6000-13500) is empty for LuAG (max point 5750); the range is deliberately 'unified across modules' (EnergyScan.C:237 comment) - keep it, but say so on the figure ('y-scale common to LuAG/DSB1/EJ-199 figures'), else it reads as wasted whitespace. 4. MINOR: spectra panel (top-left) x-range to 16000 while LuAG data end ~8000 - same shared-scale defence applies; alternatively mark the 13.6k LG headroom ceiling with a guide line to make the shared range informative. 5. MINOR: 1 GeV teal spike (0.115 fraction) compresses all other spectra below 0.03 - consider log-y or an inset. 6. NIT: timing y-scale differs from the DSB1 figure (430 vs 365 ps top), defeating at-a-glance cross-module comparison of the two crystal-like channels; unify LuAG/DSB1 timing axes as the response axes already are.
plots.physics_questions: Response panel: 7 GeV (686 ADC-eq/GeV) and 9 GeV (639) sit above the 5 GeV slope (590) - consistent with the documented gain ladder, but is the run-15-gain-corrected version (SaturationStudy bottom-right) the one that should be shown here instead of raw-as-published? sigma/E is non-monotonic (22% at 7 GeV vs 31% at 9 GeV) - worth one sentence on whether that ordering follows the beam-optics/position-smearing differences between runs or the gain ladder.

plots.what_it_shows: DSB:Ce glass 6-point energy scan, identical 2x2 grammar to the LuAG figure: spectra, response (~1350 ADC-eq/GeV, 7-11 GeV falling below the 5 GeV line), sigma/E, and shower-time sigma with 323/sqrt(E) (+) 79 ps quadrature trend.
plots.caption_issues: Same set as the LuAG figure (unlegended 11 GeV open-marker demotion, unstated quadrature fit form, undefined srCFD; EnergyScanDSB1.C:250,295 are identical clones). One DSB1-specific gap: the legend promises a 'mean of capillaries' series, but its 1 GeV point is not in the figure at all (clipped above the frame; see design issue 1) - the legend asserts data the panel does not show. Also no on-figure note that the below-line 9/11 GeV response points involve the documented LG headroom ceiling (~13.6k) and gain ladder rather than medium saturation - the retired-saturation story lives in a different figure.
plots.design_issues: 1. MAJOR (data loss): timing panel - the 1 GeV mean-of-capillaries marker is entirely absent (clipped above the ~365 ps auto-scaled frame top set by the median graph; EnergyScanDSB1.C:275-281, no SetMaximum before gm->Draw('P same')), and the teal fit curve exits the top of the frame near 1 GeV. A reader cannot tell the point was measured. Fix as for LuAG: set the y-max from the union of both graphs and the fit evaluated at 1 GeV. 2. CRITICAL (production, shared): response-panel y tick labels clipped to '2000'/'0000' - same margin bug as LuAG. 3. MAJOR (shared): subtitle 'srCFD 4-cap shower time' overprinted by the fit curve and the 1 GeV median marker (EnergyScanDSB1.C:295). 4. MINOR: DSB1 spectra extend to ~14000, i.e. through the documented 13.6k LG headroom - draw the headroom line in the spectra panel; at 9/11 GeV the upper spectral edge abuts it, which is analysis-relevant. 5. NIT: timing y-max 365 ps vs LuAG 430 ps - unify (see LuAG item 6). 6. NIT: 1 GeV legend count (22745 e) is 4-70x the other energies; the teal curve dominates panel 1 - log-y would rebalance.
plots.physics_questions: Do the 9 and 11 GeV Sum-LG spectra show truncation pile-up at the 13.6k LG headroom (the 11 GeV purple spectrum's upper edge looks compressed against ~14000)? If any fraction of 9/11 GeV events saturates LG, the peak positions in the response panel are biased low independently of the gain ladder - one sentence quantifying the fraction above 13.6k would immunise the below-line bend. The 11 GeV timing points (both estimators open, ~170-185 ps) agree with the 9 GeV median - worth noting this supports the 'contained tags are hard electrons' conclusion.

plots.what_it_shows: EJ-199 WLS 6-point energy scan, same 2x2 grammar: low response (~550-650 ADC-eq/GeV), large sigma/E, and photostatistics-limited timing (~1218/sqrt(E) ps trend, y-axis to 1500 ps - an order above the crystal channels).
plots.caption_issues: Annotations correct and conventions identical to the siblings (EnergyScanEJ199.C:250,295). Two notes: (a) '(incl. MCP+DRS)' is technically true but immaterial here since EJ-199 is photostatistics-limited - harmless; (b) nothing on the figure flags that EJ-199 is spec-mismatched to LYSO's 425 nm emission (the documented Eljen-contaminant context) - without it the figure reads as 'this material is bad' rather than 'this material was mistuned'; one caption line would prevent the misread when the three figures travel together.
plots.design_issues: 1. CRITICAL (production, shared): response-panel y tick labels clipped ('2000'/'0000') - same margin bug as the siblings. 2. MAJOR (shared): timing subtitle overlaps the teal fit curve, and here it ALSO grazes the top '1500' tick label; the 1 GeV median (~1370 ps) sits immediately under the text. Same fix: subtitle outside the frame. 3. MAJOR: width panel (bottom-left) - the 11 GeV open point (~97%, 202 e) carries an error bar spanning ~0-203%, which drags the y-axis to >200% and squashes the physically meaningful 38-75% points into the bottom quarter. Cap the axis at ~120% and let the demoted 11 GeV bar clip (with a note), or drop the point as was effectively done for its information content. 4. MINOR: response panel - the 11 GeV error bar (~4700-12800) dominates the panel; with the point already demoted, consider a lighter/dashed bar. 5. MINOR: spectra x-range to 16000 vs data ending ~11000 - shared-scale defence applies (see LuAG). 6. NIT: at 11 GeV in the timing panel, demoted-median (black open) and mean (grey open) circles nearly coincide at ~260-270 ps while the grey mean at ~390 ps has its own bar - three open circles of two meanings within 1 GeV of x; a marker-shape change for the demotion (e.g. open square) would disambiguate the whole family.
plots.physics_questions: The timing fit sits ABOVE the 5-11 GeV medians by 20-30% (curve anchored on 1 and 9 GeV; medians at 7/9/11 GeV ~270-300 ps vs curve ~400-450) - the single a/sqrt(E) (+) b form visibly fails for EJ-199; is a pure photostatistics 1/sqrt(E) with no floor, fit to all points, more honest here? Also the 3 GeV width point (74%) exceeds the 1 GeV one (46%) - non-monotonic sigma/E deserves the same one-line accounting as LuAG's.

plots.what_it_shows: Two-panel electron-tag diagnostic: (left) XCET40-XCET43 coincidence rate vs threshold per energy on log-y, with per-energy dotted cut lines (100/100/100/50/40/40) and legend; (right) XCET40 amplitude spectra per energy on log-y, showing the electron peak sliding to lower amplitude as pressure drops with beam momentum.
plots.caption_issues: 'peak slides with pressure prop-to 1/p^2' is physically right for a threshold Cherenkov tuned to keep pions sub-threshold (n-1 prop-to 1/gamma_th^2). 'plateau = clean tag' is a correct criterion, but the panel itself shows the 7, 9 and 11 GeV curves have NO plateau and their chosen cuts (50/40/40, XCETScanPlot.C:76-78) sit on steep slopes - this is the documented 11 GeV purity caveat made visible, yet the figure does not say so; a reader applying the stated criterion concludes the high-energy tags are not clean and finds no acknowledgement. Add one line ('no plateau above 5 GeV: purity degrades, see 11 GeV open markers in scan figures') or an asterisk on the affected legend entries.
plots.design_issues: 1. MAJOR: right panel - the 1 GeV (teal) and 3 GeV (gold) spectra are still rising at the x=900 edge: the electron peaks the caption is about are clipped off-canvas for the two energies where they are largest. Extend the x-range (or add overflow into the last bin and say so). 2. MAJOR: stray red mark at approximately (272 ADC-eq, 3%) in the left panel - an isolated partial marker/fragment in empty space below the legend's bottom-right corner, belonging to no curve (the red 5 GeV series ends at threshold 170). Cause not obvious in XCETScanPlot.C:66-79; investigate and remove - in print it reads as a data point. 3. MINOR: left panel x-range to 300 (XCETScanPlot.C:71) while all curves end by 280 and cuts are at 40-100; the last 20% of width is empty and the legend already crowds the 7 GeV curve's descent - trim to 280 and shift the legend. 4. MINOR: the three dotted cut lines at 100 (teal, gold, red) overprint each other into one ambiguous line; state 'cut 100' once or dodge them by +-2 ADC. 5. NIT: subtitle 'tag rate vs threshold' at (0.16,0.86) sits just above the 1 GeV curve at ~85% - close but not colliding here; same relocation as the scan figures would future-proof it. 6. NIT: canvas is 1696x612 raster; this diagnostic pair is the least print-ready of the set - vector export before any journal use.
plots.physics_questions: The 5 GeV red spectrum (right) is bimodal with a hard cluster at 600-820 well above its main body - is that the residual electron population at a pressure setting shared with a lower-energy run, or cross-talk? It matters because the 5 GeV cut of 100 was chosen off the left panel's 'plateau'. Also the 1 GeV coincidence rate plateaus at ~85%, far above the others (25%/12%) - worth stating the beam-composition numbers implied, since these rates are the denominator of the whole e-tag story.

plots.what_it_shows: Four-panel retirement of the high-energy saturation hypothesis: (1) run 30 (11 GeV) Sum-LG with all on-module tags vs centered r<0.18 subset (peak 5885+-218) and the scan containment floor; (2) peak ratio vs impact centrality per energy (transverse-leakage test); (3) MIP MPV per scan point, windowed+smoothed vs old full-window max (the gain ladder); (4) response linearity with raw-vs-centered points, linear reference, and Longo shower-max-migration curve.
plots.caption_issues: Content matches the documented conclusion (gain ladder + Longo migration, saturation retired), and panel 1's title-as-question is answered by the plot. Marked inaccurate for one concrete annotation-vs-content mismatch: panel 2's legend lists '9 GeV' (black, SaturationStudy.C:295 loop) but NO black curve or point is visible anywhere in the panel - the series either has only the reference bin (ratio identically 1, hidden under the convergence point at r~0.09) or was dropped; either way the legend promises data the panel does not show. Remove the entry or plot the point with a note. Secondary: the editorial voice ('the gain ladder, measured honestly', SaturationStudy.C:322; 'does centering restore the peak?') is fine for the campaign log but would not survive journal production - retitle descriptively ('MIP MPV per scan point, two estimators'). '5 GeV = control' in panel 2's title is unclear since every energy is normalized to its own centered peak - say what the control establishes.
plots.design_issues: 1. MAJOR: panel 2 dead legend entry (see caption). 2. MINOR: panel 2 axis framing - x runs to 0.8 with data ending at r=0.475 (40% empty width) and y spans 0.7-1.2 with data in 0.91-1.08; tighten to x<0.55, y 0.85-1.15 and the +-5-9% effects become legible. 3. MINOR: panel 1 - the grey all-tags histogram threads under the legend box (bars in the 4500-7500 region reach within a bar-width of the legend's lower edge); nudge the legend up or shrink text one step. 4. MINOR: open-vs-filled here means raw-vs-centered (panel 4) and old-vs-new estimator (panel 3), while in the scan figures it means mean-estimator or low-purity - a third and fourth semantic for the same glyph within one figure set; adopt distinct shapes per meaning family. 5. NIT: panel 3 'scan point' 1-5 is opaque without the run mapping - annotate energies or run numbers under the ticks. 6. NIT: panel 4's teal centered points are x-offset (+0.1-0.2 GeV) for dodging - fine, but at 9 GeV the raw and centered points nearly coincide and the offset makes the centered point look like it is at 9.2 GeV; state the dodge in the caption.
plots.physics_questions: Panel 2: the 3 and 7 GeV ratios go UP off-center (+8%/+4.5%) while 5 and 11 GeV go DOWN (-5%/-9%) - opposite signs with overlapping error bars; is the panel actually demonstrating 'no significant leakage trend' (in which case say that) or is the 11 GeV -9% being used as part of the halo story? Panel 4: after Longo correction the 11 GeV centered point still sits below the 9 GeV one - consistent with the documented unexplained halo, but the figure would benefit from an explicit residuals strip (data/model) to show what remains unexplained and its size.

plots.what_it_shows: Six stacked time-series over ~11.5 h since run-28 start: shower-time width (red, 'the symptom'), shower-time center, pooled HG MIP MPV (SiPM gain proxy), HG baseline RMS (dark noise), MCP amplitude, and trigger rate - the gain and noise panels show a coordinated onset at ~9 h while MCP and trigger rate stay flat, localizing the drift to the SiPMs (consistent with the documented ambient light leak / daytime effect).
plots.caption_issues: Panel labels are accurate and the '(SiPM gain)' / '(dark noise)' glosses are the right interpretive cues; '(the symptom)' is effective internally but is editorial voice for a journal. One substantive caution to carry into any caption: pooled HG MIP MPV is used here as a gain proxy, and MIP-based normalization was documented as invalid for CROSS-run gain transfer (species + noise-estimator bias) - within-run drift tracking is a legitimately different use, but the caption should say 'relative drift only' so the two conclusions cannot be conflated. Also the last shower-time-center point jumps +450 ps in the final half-hour bin - if that bin is low-statistics it should carry an error bar or be flagged.
plots.design_issues: 1. MAJOR (the missing annotation): the figure's entire argument is the ~9 h coincidence of the MPV and baseline-RMS inflections with the width blow-up, yet no shared vertical guide or shaded band marks the onset across the six panels - add one dashed line (or day/night shading, given the light-leak hypothesis) spanning all panels; it converts six plots into one argument. 2. MAJOR (house issue, confirmed): panel 2's in-frame label 'shower-time center [ps]' is struck through by the -1000 tick line at the frame's top-left (the label baseline sits exactly on the tick); panel 1's label is similarly flush against the frame. Move labels into the top margin of each pad or right-align them in the empty upper-right. 3. MINOR: no error bars anywhere - the width panel swings 200-1450 ps and the reader cannot tell scatter from drift before the 9 h onset; at minimum put bars on panels 1-2. 4. MINOR: intermediate panels each carry their own tiny x tick labels; for a shared-x stack, suppress all but the bottom panel's and enlarge those (the current ones are below print-legible size at 1496 px width for a full-column figure). 5. NIT: only panels 1-2 relate to timing yet the y-labels are inside-frame text while the scan figures use rotated axis titles - inconsistent house grammar; pick one. 6. NIT: red-vs-teal encodes symptom-vs-diagnostics - good - but the red is the same red used for '5 GeV' throughout the scan figures; within a single campaign document the double duty is worth avoiding.
plots.physics_questions: Baseline RMS doubles (50 to 100) and MIP MPV rises 60% (~220 to 350) together at ~9 h - for the light-leak hypothesis the RMS rise is natural, but a true GAIN rise (MPV) from ambient light needs the self-heating/bias-shift chain stated; is the MPV rise instead the noise pedestal leaking into the MIP fit (the same noise-estimator bias documented against MIP normalization)? Distinguishing those two changes whether timing data after 9 h are correctable or discardable. Also: does the 9 h mark correspond to local sunrise on the run-28/29 dates? One timestamp would close the loop on the untaped-module explanation.
